name: black-hat-offense

findings.title: Direct swap pricing bounds bypass via pre-fee amount stored in transient storage
confidence_deductions: Impact is bounded by token creator configuration (-15)
findings.description: In AMMStandardHook._validatePricingBounds, for direct swaps, beforeSwap stores params.amount (pre-fee input) in transient storage. afterSwap reconstructs the price using this pre-fee amount as the denominator. Since the actual swap executes with post-fee input (smaller), the computed price is systematically lower than the actual execution price by sqrt(1 - feePercent). With a 5% hook fee, the deflation is ~253 BPS, allowing direct swaps to execute at prices up to 2.5% above the configured max pricing bound.
findings.impact: Token creators who set max pricing bounds for direct swaps can have those bounds exceeded proportional to the hook fee. For tokens with 5% sell fees, the max price can be exceeded by ~2.5%. This undermines the creator's anti-sniping and price protection configuration.
findings.proof_sketch: test_H04_directSwapPreFeeAmountMismatch in AuditCrossBoundaryHypotheses.t.sol demonstrates: computeRatioX96(95e18, 100e18) < computeRatioX96(95e18, 95e18) by 253 BPS
findings.victim: Token creators who set pricing bounds for their tokens
findings.extractable_value: Proportional to fee % - attacker executes direct swaps at prices above max bound
attack_sequence: 1. Token creator sets max pricing bound for their token via registry
2. Token has a 5% sell fee configured on the hook
3. Attacker executes a direct swap at a price 2.5% above the max bound
4. beforeSwap stores pre-fee amount (100) in tstore, returns 5% fee
5. AMM deducts fee, swap executes with 95 input at target price
6. afterSwap computes price using tstore=100 denominator, gets deflated price
7. Deflated price passes max bound check even though actual price exceeds bound

findings.title: Direct swap pricing bounds bypass via pre-fee amount in transient storage
confidence_deductions: Attack path partial: bounds are advisory, not economic (-20)
findings.description: In AMMStandardHook._validatePricingBounds, for direct swaps (poolType==address(0)), beforeSwap stores params.amount (the pre-fee specified amount) in transient storage at DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT. In afterSwap, this pre-fee amount is used alongside the output amount to compute sqrtPriceX96. Since the hook fee reduces the actual input before the swap executes, the computed price ratio uses a larger denominator (pre-fee) than the actual execution price (post-fee input / output). This makes the computed price systematically lower than the true execution price, allowing swaps that execute above maxSqrtPriceX96 to pass the bounds check. For a 5% hook fee, the price discrepancy is ~5%.
findings.impact: Pricing bounds enforcement for direct swaps is weakened proportionally to the hook fee percentage. Orders that should be rejected as out-of-bounds may pass. Economic impact is indirect - pricing bounds are advisory constraints set by token creators, not economic guards on user funds.
findings.proof_sketch: See test_HR4_HH04_pricing_bounds_prefee_analysis in AuditInsolvencyKLR4.t.sol. Pre-fee input of 1000 with 5% fee (50) means actual swap uses 950 input to produce 900 output. True price ratio = 900/950 = 0.947. Computed ratio = 900/1000 = 0.9. Error = ~5%, proportional to fee.
findings.victim: Token creators who set pricing bounds
findings.extractable_value: No direct extraction - bounds are advisory. Indirect: swaps at out-of-bounds prices that token creators wanted to prevent.
attack_sequence: 1. Token creator sets maxSqrtPriceX96 at a specific price level
2. Token has 5% hook sell fee configured
3. Attacker executes direct swap at a price ~5% above the max bound
4. beforeSwap stores pre-fee amount (e.g., 1000)
5. AMM deducts 5% fee, swaps with 950 input, produces output at actual price above bound
6. afterSwap computes price using pre-fee amount (1000) as denominator, deflating the computed price
7. Deflated price passes the maxSqrtPriceX96 check even though execution price exceeds it
prerequisites: Token with non-zero hook fee for direct swaps
Pricing bounds set on token pair
code_smells: AMMStandardHook.sol:842-844 — afterSwap uses stored pre-fee amount to compute price ratio
findings.what_remains_unverified: Full integration test with deployed contracts demonstrating an actual out-of-bounds swap passing validation

findings.title: validateHandlerOrder bypasses all trading rules (pause, whitelist, direct swap block)
confidence_deductions: by-design: validateHandlerOrder is intentionally minimal for handler use
impact limited to CLOB order placement, not execution
findings.description: validateHandlerOrder has NO access control and performs NO trading rule checks (tradingIsPaused, blockDirectSwaps, pairedTokenWhitelist). Only pricing bounds are enforced. In contrast, beforeSwap/afterSwap enforce all trading rules. CLOB orders can be placed while trading is paused.
findings.impact: Token admin who pauses trading expects ALL activity to halt, but CLOB makers can continue placing orders. Orders placed during pause may fill when trading resumes.
findings.proof_sketch: test_H04_handlerOrderBypassesTradingPause: pauses trading, validateHandlerOrder succeeds, beforeSwap reverts
findings.victim: Token admins relying on trading pause for emergency stops
findings.extractable_value: Indirect - front-running advantage from placing orders during pause
attack_sequence: Token admin pauses trading due to emergency
Attacker places CLOB orders via validateHandlerOrder (no pause check)
Orders queue at favorable prices during pause
When admin unpauses, orders fill before market adjusts
